posts.title: Joe Burrow Rewrites History Books with Four More Touchdowns on Sunday Night
posts.text:
Nov 16, 2026, 12:45 AM ET
Cincinnati Bengals quarterbackJoe Burrowcompleted 35 of his 44 pass attempts for 409 yards, four passing touchdowns, and zero turnovers during Sunday's Week 10 win over the Pittsburgh Steelers. He also rushed for eight yards and took just one sack. Burrow has been absolutely magnificent lately, becoming just the second player in NFL history to record 4+ touchdowns in five consecutive games. Over his last five contests, he has posted a whopping 1,624 passing yards and 22 total touchdowns. He has also played turnover-free football in four of those five games. The former No. 1 pick has officially taken over as the overall QB1 in fantasy scoring, passing
Josh Allenfor the top spot on Sunday. Burrow has benefitted from a supporting cast headlined by
Ja'Marr Chaseand
Tee Higgins. As long as Burrow, Chase, and Higgins stay healthy, the LSU product will remain a high-end QB1 on a weekly basis. He should continue to dominate in Week 11 against the Washington Commanders, who just allowed 293 passing yards to
J.J. McCarthy.--
Andersen Pickard
Source:
RotoBaller
Start Joe Burrow This Week?
More Recent News
Andersen Pickard
Andersen Pickard
Nov 16, 2026, 12:28 AM ET
Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiverDK Metcalfcaught two of his six targets for 54 yards and one touchdown during Sunday's Week 10 loss against the Cincinnati Bengals. He also recorded an octopus, which describes when a player converts a two-point conversion immediately after scoring their own touchdown. The touchdown and two-point conversion salvaged an otherwise disappointing performance from Metcalf, who has now caught 35 of his 70 targets (50% catch rate) so far this season. His catch rate has been particularly low over his last three games, during which he has a modest five catches on 18 targets. Metcalf continues to be a low-floor WR3 in fantasy football, scoring more than 8.0 PPR points in just four of his nine games so far this season. He'll continue to rank in the WR3/flex range for Week 11 against the Philadelphia Eagles.--
Andersen Pickard
Source:
RotoBaller
Andersen Pickard
Andersen Pickard
Nov 16, 2026, 12:23 AM ET
Pittsburgh Steelers running backJaylen Warrenrushed for just 15 yards on seven carries during Sunday's Week 10 loss against the Cincinnati Bengals. He also caught five of six targets for an additional 26 receiving yards. The 28-year-old's receiving volume softened the blow a little bit in PPR leagues, but for the most part, this was an incredibly disappointing outing for someone who entered this week as a low-end RB1. His inefficiency was particularly shocking; Warren entered this week with 5.92 yards per carry, but he finished with a terrible mark of 2.14 yards per carry on Sunday night. He seemed to have no answer for the Bengals' improved run defense, and it resulted in his worst fantasy outing of the season, as well as a new season-low in carries and touches. Managers shouldn't let one dud performance derail their future lineups, so Warren should still be deployed as a high-end RB2 heading into Week 11 against a struggling Eagles team. However, Sunday revealed that his floor is likely a little lower than we previously thought.--
Andersen Pickard
Source:
RotoBaller
Andersen Pickard
Andersen Pickard
Nov 15, 2026, 11:58 PM ET
Seattle Seahawks running backJadarian Pricetotaled nine carries, 36 rushing yards, and a rushing touchdown during Sunday's Week 10 win over the Las Vegas Raiders. He also converted his lone target into an eight-yard reception. As
Zach Charbonnetcontinues to take on more volume and occupy the lead-back role, Price has seen less involvement on offense. Sunday's 10 touches were his second-lowest mark of the season, albeit over just six games. When he was coming out of college just over six months ago, the expectation was that Price's best fit was somewhere that allowed him to share the backfield responsibilities, rather than being the sole leader of the backfield. Seattle fits that description perfectly, as he has consistently logged between one-third and one-half of the snaps while still operating firmly behind Charbonnet. If not for the touchdown on Sunday, Price would have gone down as a bust this week. However, he was able to find the end zone and has now posted double-digit fantasy points (PPR) in back-to-back games. He'll rank as an RB3/flex option in 12+ team leagues on the other side of the Seahawks' Week 11 bye.--
Andersen Pickard
Source:
RotoBaller
Andersen Pickard
Andersen Pickard
Nov 15, 2026, 11:32 PM ET
New York Jets wide receiverGarrett Wilsoncaught seven of his 14 targets for 106 yards during Sunday's Week 10 loss against the Buffalo Bills. He also lost a fumble. Wilson, who missed Week 9 with a concussion, returned to action after a one-game absence and didn't seem to miss a beat. He didn't find the end zone, but he did lead the Jets in targets, catches, and receiving yards. The 26-year-old was able to turn in an impressive performance despite some quarterback instability, as
Geno Smith(head, ankle) exited twice and
Cade Klubnikended up attempting 20 passes. Wilson has managed to rank as a low-end WR1 despite the Jets' subpar offensive results and their 2-8 record this year. He may have a slightly lower floor next week if Klubnik has to start in place of Smith, but even in that hypothetical scenario, he'd still be a mid-to-high WR2 option. After all, Wilson converted eight targets from Klubnik into four receptions, so more than half of his volume came with the backup in the game.--
Andersen Pickard
Source:
RotoBaller
Andersen Pickard
Andersen Pickard
Nov 15, 2026, 11:00 PM ET
Jacksonville Jaguars quarterbackTrevor Lawrencecompleted 25 of his 35 pass attempts for 352 yards, three passing touchdowns, and one interception during Sunday's Week 10 win over the Tennessee Titans. He also rushed for an additional 27 yards on four attempts. Lawrence's remarkable season continues, as he has now recorded 3+ touchdowns in five of his nine games so far this year. Sunday showed that the former No. 1 pick is capable of racking up fantasy points regardless of his matchup, including in extremely positive game script scenarios like this week against Tennessee. The only real blemish on Lawrence's season is the fact that he has a turnover in four of his last five games, but on a more positive note, he hasn't had a multi-turnover game yet this season. Managers should confidently deploy Lawrence as a mid-range QB1 option for next Sunday against the New York Giants in Week 11.--
Andersen Pickard
Source:
RotoBaller
Andy Webb
Andy Webb
Nov 15, 2026, 10:47 PM ET
Tennessee Titans wide receiverWan'Dale Robinson(ankle) was unable to find much success during Sunday's matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars. The Titans were without
Carnell Tate(shoulder), so the expectation was that Robinson would have a bigger impact. Instead, Robinson struggled with only three receptions on four targets for 10 yards in the loss. He also exited the contest due to an ankle injury. It doesn't sound like it's anything serious, but fantasy managers should monitor his status ahead of the Week 11 matchup against the Dallas Cowboys. Robinson has been held to under 25 receiving yards in three of his last four games. He should bounce back against the struggling Cowboys defense. If he doesn't play,
Elic Ayomanorand
Chimere Dikecould see larger roles.--
Andy Webb
Source:
ESPN
Andy Webb
Andy Webb
Nov 15, 2026, 10:38 PM ET
New York Jets running backBraelon Allenwas once again an afterthought in the offense on Sunday. Allen was running wild on opposing defense when
Breece Hallwas out, but now he's struggling to make a significant impact. In Week 10, Allen carried the ball eight times for 40 yards and hauled in his lone target for six yards in the loss. This marks the second straight week that Allen has been held to under 10 carries. He continues to run the ball well, but his role is limited with Hall back in the mix. Hall is also the preferred receiving back, and the Jets are passing a lot when they're playing from behind. Fantasy managers should expect Allen to remain involved, but he won't be an ideal starting option going forward. He might offer some deep league value against the Los Angeles Chargers, who are still seeking their first win in Week 11.--
Andy Webb
Source:
ESPN
Andersen Pickard
Andersen Pickard
Nov 15, 2026, 10:32 PM ET
Dallas Cowboys wide receiverCeeDee Lambcaught seven of his 13 targets for 72 yards and one touchdown during Sunday's Week 10 loss against the San Francisco 49ers. Lamb got off to a very quiet start on Sunday, as he didn't catch his first pass until there were less than two minutes left in the first half. However, once he got going, he was nearly unstoppable. The star receiver caught six passes in the second half alone, including a touchdown in the final minute that pulled Dallas within six points of San Francisco. He trailed
George Pickensin overall production, as Pickens exploded for 11 catches, 145 yards, and three touchdowns. However, Lamb still racked up more than 20 points in PPR leagues, and he has now scored at least 12.8 points in nine of his 10 games so far this year. Dallas loves to throw the ball while consistently finding itself in close games, so there should be no shortage of targets and big plays for Lamb going forward. He'll remain a mid-to-high WR1 option heading into Week 11 against the Titans, who just surrendered 152 yards and one touchdown to
Parker Washington.--
Andersen Pickard
Source:
RotoBaller
Deebo Samuel Sr. Makes a Statement in Return
Andy Webb
Andy Webb
Nov 15, 2026, 10:29 PM ET
San Francisco 49ers wide receiverDeebo Samuel Sr.made his return to the field after missing each of the last three games. The veteran wideout made a splash during his return against the Dallas Cowboys this weekend. He hauled in all three of his targets for 31 yards and a touchdown. Samuel also rushed the ball three times for 78 yards and another score on the ground. The 30-year-old was a big part of the 49ers' victory on Sunday. He has now found the end zone in three of his last four games. The 49ers are extremely banged up at wide receiver, so Samuel figures to remain an important part of the offense for next week's matchup against the Minnesota Vikings.--
Andy Webb
Source:
ESPN
Andersen Pickard
Andersen Pickard
Nov 15, 2026, 10:26 PM ET
Carolina Panthers running backChuba Hubbardtotaled 27 carries, 92 rushing yards, and two rushing touchdowns during Sunday's Week 10 win over the New Orleans Saints. He also converted five targets into five catches for 80 receiving yards. Hubbard had a remarkable game as he led the Panthers in carries, rushing yards, catches, and receiving yards. He was also responsible for both of the team's touchdowns. The 27-year-old continued to produce like a true workhorse back, and he solidified himself as a strong RB1 option in fantasy football. As players like
Tetairoa McMillanand
Jalen Cokercontinue to turn in modest performances, Hubbard is proving that the entire offense runs through him. He has posted double-digit fantasy points (PPR) in all nine of his games this season. Even if
Jonathon Brooks(core) returns from injured reserve in the next few days, Hubbard should continue to be started in 100% of leagues heading into another favorable matchup against the Ravens in Week 11.--
Andersen Pickard
Source:
RotoBaller
Andy Webb
Andy Webb
Nov 15, 2026, 10:20 PM ET
Las Vegas Raiders running backAshton Jeantycontinued his lackluster performance on the ground during Sunday's game against the Seattle Seahawks. Jeanty carried the ball nine times for 18 yards as he continues to find no room to run. This marks the sixth straight game that Jeanty has finished with fewer than 30 rushing yards. He was able to somewhat salvage his fantasy value with four receptions for 46 yards through the air in the loss. Due to Jeanty's lack of success,
Mike Washington Jr.has seen a bigger role in the offense lately. The expectation is that the two of them will continue to split up the duties going forward. Jeanty will remain a frustrating fantasy option ahead of the Week 11 matchup against the Denver Broncos.--
Andy Webb
Source:
ESPN
Ryan O'Bleness
Ryan O'Bleness
Nov 15, 2026, 10:18 PM ET
Minnesota Vikings wide receiverJustin Jeffersonearned 13 targets and recorded nine receptions for 74 yards (8.2 yards per catch) in a 30-10 win over the Green Bay Packers in Week 10. In Jefferson's first game in 2026 in which he played with newly-acquired quarterback
Kirk Cousins, Jefferson set new season highs in both targets and receptions, while the 74 yards were his third-most of the season. Of course, Cousins and Jefferson already have a strong connection after playing together in Minnesota from 2020 until 2023. Jefferson and the Vikings are hoping that Cousins is the answer to the team's quarterback woes, and he was solid on Sunday, completing 21 out of 31 passes for 207 yards, two touchdowns and an interception against the Packers. It's been a frustrating year for Jefferson, individually, due to subpar quarterback play from
Kyler Murrayand
Carson Wentz, but Jefferson remains one of the most talented wide receivers in the league, and Cousins raises his ceiling significantly. The Vikings are now 7-2 in the 2026 season, thanks in large part to their defense, and Minnesota may have found the solution on offense.--
Ryan O'Bleness
Source:
NFL.com
Andy Webb
Andy Webb
Nov 15, 2026, 10:11 PM ET
Arizona Cardinals running backTyler Allgeiergave fantasy managers a dud during Sunday's game against the Los Angeles Rams. Allgeier was hopeful for better results after struggling last week, but he actually did worse this weekend. On Sunday, Allgeier carried the ball five times for 14 yards and failed to haul in his lone target in the loss. The five touches in the backfield were the fewest for Allgeier since Week 5. Fellow back
Bam Knightreturned this weekend, but he didn't do much better with five carries for 19 yards. The Cardinals offense couldn't get anything going at all with quarterback
Carson Beckmaking his first career start. The hope is that Allgeier and this Cardinals' offense can rebound against the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 11.--
Andy Webb
Source:
ESPN
Ryan O'Bleness
Ryan O'Bleness
Nov 15, 2026, 10:00 PM ET
Carolina Panthers wide receiverTetairoa McMillanrecorded three receptions (on seven targets) for 35 yards (11.7 yards per reception) and no touchdowns in a 20-17 win over the New Orleans Saints in Week 10. While McMillan led the team in targets, he finished third in receptions and third in receiving yards behind running back
Chuba Hubbard(five receptions for 80 yards) and tight end
Tommy Tremble(four catches for 48 yards). Quarterback
Bryce Youngwas held to 200 passing yards against the New Orleans defense, so McMillan's low production is not a surprise. Still, the three catches and 35 yards marked the lowest totals for McMillan since Week 3 (two catches for 17 yards versus the Cleveland Browns). McMillan will continue to operate as Carolina's WR1, and there should not be many concerns about his production or usage moving forward.--
Ryan O'Bleness
Source:
NFL.com
Will Brady
Will Brady
Nov 15, 2026, 9:58 PM ET
Kansas City Chiefs quarterbackPatrick Mahomesput together a vintage performance in his team's Week 10 blowout of the Atlanta Falcons, completing 22 of 35 pass attempts for 348 yards, five touchdowns, and zero interceptions. Across nine games this season, the 31-year-old has now thrown for 2,385 yards, 19 touchdowns, and four interceptions. Mahomes has quietly played some of his best football of the season lately, throwing for 911 yards, 10 touchdowns, and zero interceptions over his last three games. The Chiefs also added a legitimate pass-catching weapon at the trade deadline in wide receiver
Josh Downs, who had four catches for 53 yards and a touchdown on five targets in his first game with Kansas City. Mahomes profiles as a must-start fantasy quarterback heading into a favorable Week 11 matchup against the Arizona Cardinals.--
Will Brady
Source:
ESPN.com
Javonte Williams Has Limited Impact in High-Scoring Affair Vs. 49ers
Ryan O'Bleness
Ryan O'Bleness
Nov 15, 2026, 9:49 PM ET
Dallas Cowboys running backJavonte Williamsrushed 16 times for 63 yards (3.9 yards per carry), while catching his lone target for four yards in a 46-40 loss to the San Francisco 49ers in Week 10. Williams did not find the end zone. The game was high-scoring throughout, and the Cowboys were down 38-19 early in the fourth quarter, so the game script called for 51 passing attempts from Dallas quarterback
Dak Prescott, and Williams had fewer opportunities in the running game. Williams was coming off a Week 9 performance of 20 carries for 101 yards (5.05 yards per carry) and a touchdown, along with four receptions for 23 yards (5.8 yards per catch) in a win over the Indianapolis Colts. While it wasn't the most efficient or productive performance for Williams in Week 10, fantasy managers do not need to worry, as he remains a high-volume RB1.--
Ryan O'Bleness
Source:
NFL.com
Will Brady
Will Brady
Nov 15, 2026, 9:47 PM ET
Seattle Seahawks running backZach Charbonnetwas his team's leading rusher in their Week 10 win over the Las Vegas Raiders, recording 20 carries for 94 yards. The 25-year-old was held out of the end zone, which led to an underwhelming day for fantasy managers. Still, Charbonnet appears to be the clear lead back in Seattle, as he out-touched Seahawks rookie rusher
Jadarian Price20 to 10 against Las Vegas. Across three games since returning from the torn ACL that ended his 2025 campaign, Charbonnet has recorded 42 carries for 194 yards and hauled in four catches for 15 yards on six targets. If Charbonnet can start scoring touchdowns, he could move into top-24 running back territory for fantasy managers following Seattle's Week 11 bye.--
Will Brady
Source:
ESPN.com
Will Brady
Will Brady
Nov 15, 2026, 9:40 PM ET
Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiverParker Washingtonwas one of the stars of his team's 40-23 win over the Tennessee Titans in Week 10, recording seven catches for 152 yards and a touchdown on nine targets. Entering Week 10, Washington had been held under 65 receiving yards and five receptions in three straight games. Still, the 24-year-old is in the midst of a breakout season. Across nine games, Washington has hauled in 36 catches for 645 yards and six touchdowns on 64 targets. The Jaguars offense also looks like one of the best units in the NFL, as Jacksonville has averaged 36.5 points per game in their last four contests. Washington profiles as a must-start wide receiver for fantasy managers heading into his Week 11 matchup against the New York Giants.--
Will Brady
Source:
ESPN.com
Ryan O'Bleness
Ryan O'Bleness
Nov 15, 2026, 9:36 PM ET
Rookie first-round wide receiverJordyn Tysonrecorded 11 receptions (on 13 targets) for 80 yards in the New Orleans Saints' 20-17 loss to the Carolina Panthers in Week 10. Tyson, the No. 8 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, led the Saints in targets, receptions and receiving yards against the Panthers, while, unsurprisingly, recording new career highs in each category. After missing the first seven games of the 2026 season, Tyson made his debut in a Week 9 win over the Cleveland Browns and recorded four receptions (on five targets) for 30 yards (7.5 yards per catch). After playing just 18 offensive snaps last week against the Browns, Tyson saw a large increase in Week 10, playing 45 snaps against the Panthers. Tyson is currently rostered in just 58% of Yahoo leagues and is certainly worth picking up if available. Tyson has WR3 or flex appeal in a Week 11 matchup against the Chicago Bears next week.--
Ryan O'Bleness
Source:
NFL.com
Keith Hernandez
Keith Hernandez
Nov 15, 2026, 9:32 PM ET
Las Vegas Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak said that star tight endBrock Bowers(ankle) will be re-evaluated on Monday, according to Ryan McFadden of ESPN. Bowers injured his ankle early in the first quarter of Sunday's 21-13 loss to the visiting Seattle Seahawks before attempting to re-enter the game, but he eventually headed to the locker room and was ruled out for the rest of the contest. In rookie quarterback
Fernando Mendoza's first NFL start, Bowers caught only two passes for 18 yards. Running back
Ashton Jeantywas the Raiders' leading receiver with four catches (four targets) for 46 yards. Until we know more about the 23-year-old Bowers' ankle injury, fantasy managers should consider him questionable to play in a Week 11 divisional matchup on the road in Denver against the first-place Broncos. With Bowers banged up, tight end
Michael Mayerwill be a popular waiver-wire target going into Week 11. Mayer caught two of his three targets from Mendoza against Seattle for 16 yards. Bowers is a must-start in all fantasy football leagues if healthy, but managers need to prepare for the possibility that he will not be available next Sunday against the Broncos, which would be bad news for Mendoza's value in two-QB superflex leagues.--
Keith Hernandez

Radnor|Local Event
Radnor EAC Lecture Series: Putting Plants to Work with Refugia Design's Jeff Lorenz
Radnor EAC Lecture Series:
Putting Plants to Work with Refugia Design's Jeff Lorenz
In partnership with Radnor Memorial Library
Tuesday, Dec 8th, 2026 7pm Winsor Room
Extreme weather means more extreme stormwater runoff - one of the most common issues facing homeowners in our area. How can we get creative with landscape design, plant choices and materials to create a beautiful and multi-functional outdoor space? Reducing lawn, establishing deep-rooted plantings, and integrating permeable hardscaping is key to reducing erosion in our neighborhoods, filtering pollutants, and absorbing dirty water before it enters our waterways.
Join Jeff Lorenz, founder of Refugia Design, for expert strategies and insight on creating native habitat that is immersive, functional, and resilient. Drawing on Refugia's award-winning Greenway Network, a GIS-mapped system of 300+ connected native landscapes, he'll show how the right plantings solve problems and how individual projects can add up to landscape-scale impact on habitat and stormwater across entire communities.
Bring your stormwater and all other garden related questions for Jeff and let's put our plants to work!
There is no registration. We hope you’ll join us.
The Radnor Township Environmental Advisory Council serves as a clearinghouse for issues of any environmental nature. The EAC recommends plans and programs to the appropriate Township agencies for identification and resolution of environmental problems.

posts.title: Roche's Gazyva/Gazyvaro becomes the first FDA-approved treatment for primary membranous nephropathy | RHHBY Stock News
posts.text:
Roche’s Gazyva/Gazyvaro becomes the first FDA-approved treatment for primary membranous nephropathy
Sentiment and the balance of points
Rhea-AI Sentiment reads the wording of the document, how positive or negative its language is on a 1 to 5 scale. The balance of points shown with the takes weighs what the document actually discloses, so the two can disagree, for example when a trial that missed its main goal is described in upbeat language.
Rhea-AI Summary
Roche (RHHBY) received FDA approval for Gazyva/Gazyvaro to treat adults with primary membranous nephropathy at risk of disease progression. The approval is to induce remission of proteinuria, or high urine protein levels, making it the first FDA-approved therapy for this disease.
In the phase III MAJESTY trial, complete remission at 104 weeks reached 36.1% versus 5.7% with tacrolimus (p<0.001). Overall remission at 104 weeks was 50% versus 12.9%, while complete remission at week 76 was 36.1% versus 8.6%. No new safety signals were identified. Data are being submitted to other global health authorities, including the European Medicines Agency.
For systemic lupus erythematosus, Roche expects an FDA decision by December 2026. A European advisory committee has recommended approval, with a final European Commission decision expected in the near future.

AI-generated analysis. How Rhea-AI works. Not financial advice.
- Approval based on phase III MAJESTY results demonstrating Gazyva/Gazyvaro superiority over tacrolimus in achieving complete remission of proteinuria at two years (
36.1% vs.5.7% ; p<0.001) - Primary membranous nephropathy (pMN) is a rare, chronic autoimmune disease; when left untreated, up to
30% of patients progress to kidney failure within
10 years - This approval further strengthens Gazyva/Gazyvaro’s role across multiple immune-mediated kidney diseases and reinforces the potential of B cell-driven innovation in nephrology and rheumatology
Basel, 16 November 2026 – Roche (SIX: RO, ROP; OTCQX: RHHBY) announced today that the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved Gazyva®/Gazyvaro® (obinutuzumab) for the treatment of adult patients with primary membranous nephropathy (pMN) at risk of disease progression, to induce remission of proteinuria. Gazyva/Gazyvaro becomes the first and only therapy to receive FDA approval for this disease, having previously been granted Breakthrough Therapy Designation. A chronic autoimmune disease that can lead to kidney failure, pMN carries a substantial human and economic burden for patients, caregivers and health systems alike.1,2 Proteinuria is a key indicator of kidney damage characterised by high urine protein levels.
“The FDA approval of Gazyva/Gazyvaro represents an important step forward for people living with primary membranous nephropathy, where targeting B cells addresses a critical underlying driver of disease,” said Levi Garraway, MD, PhD, Roche’s Chief Medical Officer and Head of Global Product Development. “With Gazyva/Gazyvaro, we are turning decades of specialised antibody engineering into tangible outcomes for patients with immune-mediated kidney diseases. By achieving significantly higher complete remission rates compared to tacrolimus, Gazyva/Gazyvaro offers a more effective approach to help achieve durable
disease control.”
The approval is based on positive results from the phase III MAJESTY study.3 The trial met its primary endpoint, with New England Journal of Medicine (NEJM). Data are also being submitted to other global health authorities, including the European Medicines Agency.
“People living with primary membranous nephropathy face the risk of progressive kidney damage and significant uncertainty about their health,” said Marc Hurlbert, PhD, Chief Executive Officer of the National Kidney Foundation. “The first FDA approval of a treatment specifically for this condition is a milestone, finally giving patients and clinicians more treatment options. Our hope is that the approval of Gazyva/Gazyvaro provides a turning point for people navigating pMN.”
pMN is a rare, chronic autoimmune condition that causes potentially irreversible kidney damage and can lead to kidney failure. People living with pMN often experience fatigue, edema (swelling) and significant emotional and social challenges that deeply affect both patients and their families.1,4 Beyond the individual impact, pMN places a substantial burden on healthcare systems.2,5 Achieving complete remission is important to help maintain kidney function and delay or prevent the onset of serious and potentially fatal complications.2
“pMN can lead to debilitating physical and psychological symptoms that place a heavy burden on patients, families and healthcare systems alike,” said Teresa Graham, Chief Executive Officer, Roche Pharmaceuticals. “This first-ever FDA approval delivers an important targeted treatment option for the pMN community and expands how many people may benefit from Gazyva/Gazyvaro across multiple severe immune-mediated kidney diseases.”
This is the third FDA approval of Gazyva/Gazyvaro in immune-mediated kidney diseases, following approvals in idiopathic nephrotic syndrome (INS) and lupus nephritis (LN). The FDA is currently evaluating Gazyva/Gazyvaro for adults with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and is expected to make a decision by December 2026. Additionally, the European Medicines Agency’s Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use (CHMP) recently issued a positive opinion recommending the approval of Gazyva/Gazyvaro for adults with SLE, with a final decision from the European Commission expected in the near future. Beyond Gazyva/Gazyvaro, Roche has a broad pipeline to bring breakthrough innovation across immunology, including immune-mediated kidney diseases.
About Gazyva/Gazyvaro
Gazyva®/Gazyvaro® (obinutuzumab) is a humanised monoclonal antibody designed with a Type II anti-CD20 region for direct B cell death, and a glycoengineered Fc region for higher binding affinity and increased antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC).6 CD20 is a protein found on certain types of B cells. Gazyva/Gazyvaro is approved for adults with lupus nephritis in more than 65 countries, and for idiopathic nephrotic syndrome in adults and paediatric patients in the US. Gazyva/Gazyvaro is also approved in 100 countries for various types of haematological cancers.
About the MAJESTY study
MAJESTY [NCT04629248] is a phase III, randomised, open-label, multicentre study designed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of Gazyva®/Gazyvaro® (obinutuzumab) in adults with primary membranous nephropathy. The study enrolled 142 adults who were randomised 1:1 to receive Gazyva/Gazyvaro or tacrolimus. The primary endpoint is the percentage of adults who achieve complete remission of proteinuria at two years (week 104).
About primary membranous nephropathy
Primary membranous nephropathy is a chronic autoimmune condition where the body’s immune system attacks the filtering units of the kidney, the glomeruli, causing protein to leak into the urine and potentially a gradual decline in kidney function. Over time, the damage to the kidneys can become irreversible, increasing the risk of life-threatening complications, such as kidney failure, idiopathic nephrotic syndrome, blood clots and cardiovascular diseases. Achieving complete remission is important to help maintain kidney function and delay or prevent the onset of serious and potentially fatal complications.
Primary membranous nephropathy has an estimated incidence of 1.2 per 100,000 people in the United States per year.7
About Roche in Immunology
For over two decades, Roche has advanced immune system research, creating groundbreaking targeted treatments that have transformed care for people with blood disorders, neurological conditions and autoimmune diseases. With a development pipeline exploring more than 20 medical approaches, we are targeting widespread, complex conditions like chronic lung disease (COPD) and inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), alongside lupus and autoimmune kidney diseases. Our ultimate goal is to lessen the burden of chronic immune disorders on patients, healthcare systems, and society.

Who is eligible for Roche’s Gazyva/Gazyvaro under the FDA primary membranous nephropathy approval?
The FDA approved Gazyva/Gazyvaro for adults with primary membranous nephropathy at risk of disease progression, to induce remission of proteinuria. Proteinuria means high levels of protein in the urine and is an indicator of kidney damage.
How did Roche’s Gazyva/Gazyvaro compare with tacrolimus in the MAJESTY trial?
Complete remission of proteinuria at two years, or 104 weeks, occurred in 36.1% of adults receiving Gazyva/Gazyvaro versus 5.7% receiving tacrolimus (p<0.001). The trial met its primary endpoint and also showed superiority on the reported secondary remission endpoints.
How was Roche’s MAJESTY trial of Gazyva/Gazyvaro designed?
MAJESTY was a phase III, randomised, open-label, multicentre study enrolling 142 adults with primary membranous nephropathy. Participants were assigned 1:1 to Gazyva/Gazyvaro or tacrolimus. Open-label means the treatment assignments were not concealed.

posts.title: 'Even a snail would agree': Thunberg's Aussie verdict - The Australian Museum Blog
posts.text:
Environmental activist Greta Thunberg has slammed Australia's track record on climate action at COP31 talks in Turkey, saying "even a snail would agree" that the country needs to move faster.
The 23-year-old Swedish woman's appearance alongside speakers from Australia, Nepal, Rwanda and Gaza caused traffic chaos inside the United Nations' climate summit in Antalya on Thursday, which also heard criticism of Australia's ongoing mining approvals.
Australia's Energy Minister Chris Bowen will lead negotiations at the annual event, which has drawn more than 92,000 attendees, and Prime Minister Anthony Albanese arrived on Wednesday for the leaders' summit portion of the event.
Asked whether she agreed with comments about Australia's slow record on climate action, Ms Thunberg said her opinion was obvious.
"Even a snail would agree with that," she told the crowd.
"It's commonsense. It doesn't get more clear than that."
Ms Thunberg previously spoke at the event in 2018 and 2019 but criticised the COP26 event in 2021, describing it as "blah, blah, blah".
She returned to bring attention to the state of the climate, she said, and call for action to prevent further disasters.
"We are all here because we know that the climate crisis is already here and now, and it is already a matter of life and death," Ms Thunberg said.
"And these disastrous trends we are seeing unfold all over the world are going to continue to exponentially get worse and worse.
"We have to start acting accordingly."
Indigenous woman Rikki Dank also spoke at the event, saying Mr Albanese should listen to calls from Traditional Owners to stop approving new and extended fossil fuel projects.
"He needs to stop speaking and start listening to the Australian people when they say no more new coal, oil and gas," she said.
"He needs to stop speaking and start listening to our brothers and sisters across the world when they say they don't want us to export coal, oil or gas and the climate harms that they bring with them."
Mr Albanese and Mr Bowen have so far declined to address proposals to transition away from fossil fuels at the COP31 event, instead discussing electrification and renewable energy targets.

posts.title: Institutional Alignment Needed to Add Underutilized Nutritious Crops to
posts.text:
Mainstreaming nutritious underutilized species into the Ghana School Feeding Programme represents an institutional alignment problem rather than a simple menu-design challenge, according to an exploratory qualitative political economy case study published in Frontiers in Sustainable Food Systems. Conducted by researchers from the University of Health and Allied Sciences in Ghana, Imperial College London, and the University of Johannesburg, the research examined why political commitments to dietary diversity and agrobiodiversity fail to translate automatically into routine school food procurement and meal delivery.
To investigate the political economy surrounding the national school feeding framework, the study examined five interrelated operational dimensions: institutional mandates, financing structures, public food procurement models, actor incentives, and available policy levers.
The study’s qualitative findings were drawn from eighty-four stakeholder participant-engagements representing diverse institutional levels rather than unique individual participants. Fieldwork and data collection encompassed four structured collaborative mechanisms: a national Net-Map exercise involving fourteen participants, a district-level stakeholder engagement session involving thirty-six participants, six key informant interviews, and a multi-level scenario-building panel session that convened twenty-eight participants. The participating individuals represented an extensive range of institutional and stakeholder groups, including national government agencies, frontline school feeding actors, agricultural institutions, academic research organisations, civil society organisations, community representatives, international development partners, and commercial private-sector food actors.
Through thematic analysis of the stakeholder engagements, the researchers identified seven interrelated mechanisms that constrain the mainstreaming of nutritious underutilized species within the school feeding system. These structural barriers include fragmented institutional mandates among government bodies; delayed and unpredictable payment disbursements from the state; local procurement arrangements that prioritize operational convenience and short-term liquidity; caterer pre-financing combined with the downward transfer of financial risk; weak commercial linkages between farmers and caterers; limited school and community accountability and oversight; and agricultural system lock-ins that sustain conventional staple production.
Severe payment delays and unpredictable disbursement schedules exhaust caterers’ working capital, transferring financial risks directly onto caterers who are forced to pre-finance daily meal preparation. Caterers therefore rely heavily on lower-risk conventional staple foods and purchase supplies from commercial traders who provide flexible credit arrangements, preventing the routine procurement of diverse, nutritious underutilized crops.
On the agricultural supply side, the investigation highlighted systemic disincentives that discourage local smallholders from cultivating nutritious underutilized species for school feeding. Smallholder farmers face uncertain and unpredictable institutional demand, compounded by seasonal harvest fluctuations, inadequate post-harvest storage facilities, and weak rural aggregation systems. These compounding factors reinforce agricultural system lock-ins, ensuring that high-level policy support for agrobiodiversity and sustainable diets fails to stimulate routine farm production or market integration.
The authors concluded that successfully mainstreaming nutritious underutilized species requires resolving institutional misalignments across governance tiers, public financing mechanisms, and frontline operational incentives. Meaningful progress requires providing reliable and predictable financing to eliminate caterer pre-financing burdens and formally incorporating nutritious underutilized species into official menu guidelines and public procurement directives. Furthermore, the researchers outlined the need for decentralized district procurement platforms, improved farmer aggregation and storage infrastructure, seasonal nutrient-equivalent substitution rules, structured farmer-caterer contractual arrangements, strengthened school and community oversight, and enhanced cross-sector coordination supported by adaptive learning processes.
Ultimately, the researchers emphasized that public school meal procurement can support nutrition security, agrobiodiversity, and local agricultural livelihoods only when governance structures, financing flows, and frontline incentives are deliberately aligned.

posts.title: Volunteers sought for Springfield Christkindlmarket plans - NewsBreak
posts.text:
By Dave DeMille ,
2 days ago
Springfield's planned German-style Christmas market is moving into its next stage as organizers recruit volunteers to help shape the Christkindlmarket scheduled for 2027.
Planning committees are now being formed, according to a community announcement, and people interested in taking part can sign up at forms.gle/Zg3Q7T4fmXL1xbuv9 .
The planned Christkindlmarket would bring a free-admission holiday market with vendors selling food and crafts to downtown Springfield. Similar German-style markets operate elsewhere in the Midwest, including Chicago and other central Illinois cities.
Downtown Springfield Inc. Director Jay Shanle discussed the project at the Springfield City Council meeting in July . DSI previously said the Christkindlmarket would complement, rather than replace, the city's existing Old Capitol Holiday Walks.
Organizers are also preparing to celebrate this season's Old Capitol Holiday Walks.
